current_round.prompt:
Make text in the shared terminal reliably selectable and copyable, including Agent and Custom Skill tabs and retained output after a process exits.

The request remains valid. Current main has clipboard shortcuts and error messages but lacks the retained candidate's selection hints, Copy selection control and recovery field for blocked clipboard access. Round 1 produced 7f6988c7 with 71 recorded focused checks passing, then refreshed it to be1f6f0366dd855f93f505d470dd4e2ca5c6d1b5. The refreshed candidate failed its evaluation and is not integrated into main; the earlier pass does not approve that replacement. Its worktree is clean and retained.

Review and selectively port that candidate's shared clipboard behavior. Explain Shift-drag on Windows/Linux and Option-drag on macOS when the application captures the mouse. Provide an accessible Copy selection control, native copy and focused platform shortcuts that use the originating terminal's selection even after exit or disconnection. Preserve Ctrl+C interruption without selection, paste framing, duplicate-event prevention and session replacement checks.

When browser clipboard writes are unavailable or rejected, attempt supported fallbacks and offer the captured text in a normal selectable field. Report success only after a successful copy, retain the user's selection and keep asynchronous results attached to their originating tab. Do not disrupt input or focus in another tab. Custom Skills now use the shared agent-tab lifecycle, so test that surface explicitly as well as ordinary Agent tabs.

Reconcile tests with current main f880b776 and its browser-fixture and rendered-output fixes. The old candidate's tests/support/web_app.js and test-file restructuring are not authoritative; retain only changes needed for this behavior. Run focused browser checks with actual Chromium and report any skips as skips. Verify selection gestures, copy after exit, denied clipboard access, tab switching, keyboard focus, interruption, exactly-once paste and retained rendering against the final candidate using current Skill verification.

This is a recovery Round following the Skills review on 10 September 2026. Start from current main in a new managed Round worktree. Preserve Round 1, its plans, logs, branches, commits and uncommitted files; inspect and selectively reuse useful work instead of replaying the whole old attempt. Use the current Skills and docs/intent contracts, not archived Governance, Quality or Guidance configuration or the old fixed planning sequence. Refine owns workflow advancement and integration; human approval remains separate. Update only affected documentation and report focused verification with actual results.

result.summary: The plan covers shared terminal selection, reliable copying, retained output, and clipboard failure recovery.

checklist.description: Make text selectable when terminal applications capture mouse input by retaining Shift-drag on Windows and Linux, enabling Option-drag on macOS, and displaying a concise selection hint while preserving ordinary application mouse handling.

Move shared terminal clipboard behavior into a focused browser module that routes Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Shift+C, Cmd+C, native Copy events, and the Copy control through the originating terminal's selection without requiring a live process.

Add a keyboard-accessible Copy selection control to the shared terminal header whose enabled state follows the current selection, works with retained output, and preserves the originating tab, selection, and renderer.

Keep shortcuts scoped to the focused terminal, preserve Ctrl+C interruption without a selection, and retain existing terminal-native paste framing, duplicate-event prevention, and session replacement guards.

Provide browser-supported fallbacks for unavailable or rejected clipboard writes, show success only when the copy operation reports success, and offer the captured selection in a standard selectable field with actionable feedback when automatic copying remains blocked, keeping recovery attached to the originating tab without disrupting another tab.

Update the existing Terminal intent page in its established format to describe selection gestures, the Copy control, focused shortcut behavior, copying retained output, and clipboard failure recovery.

result.summary: Make selected text in Agent windows easy to copy through the shared terminal surface by exposing selection gestures and a Copy selection control, allowing copying after exit or disconnection, and providing recoverable clipboard failures while preserving terminal input behavior.

governance_precheck.message: Executing the finalized plan as written does not require violating any supplied governance rule or enabled guidance.

checklist.evidence: Enabled macOptionClickForcesSelection and displayed a platform-specific drag hint. Real xterm tests verified Shift-drag on Linux and Option-drag with a simulated Mac platform under mouse capture, while ordinary mouse input still reached the application.

Extracted shared copy/paste behavior into the focused 291-line terminal-clipboard.js module and loaded it in index.html. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Shift+C, Cmd+C, native Copy, and the control capture the originating renderer's selection without requiring a live session.

Added a native keyboard-accessible Copy selection header button whose disabled state follows xterm selection changes. Browser tests verified keyboard activation, exited/sessionless copying, and renderer/selection retention across tab changes. Selected output and unfinished copy recovery defer automatic restart; the explicit Restart action remains available.

Clipboard shortcuts require focus inside the active terminal. Verified Ctrl+C interruption without selection, terminal-native multiline bracketed paste exactly once, unchanged Agent Ctrl+Enter/Ctrl+Z behavior, and existing asynchronous/buffered paste session replacement guards.

Clipboard API success, native Copy handling, or a true execCommand result is required before reporting success. Unavailable, throwing, and rejected writes use a selection fallback; failed fallbacks expose captured text in a labeled readonly textarea with Select text and Dismiss controls. Delayed results are fenced to the original attempt, renderer, and session. Tests verified recovery remains on an exited originating tab and preserves another tab's focus, plus manual-field selection across Toolbar redraws.

Updated only docs/intent/05-surfaces/03-browser/19-terminal.md, preserving its established sections and documenting selection gestures, Copy selection, focused shortcuts, retained output, and manual recovery.

rounds.prompt:
Make text in the shared terminal reliably selectable and copyable, including Agent and Custom Skill tabs and retained output after a process exits.

The request remains valid. Review and selectively port that candidate's shared clipboard behavior. Explain Shift-drag on Windows/Linux and Option-drag on macOS when the application captures the mouse. Provide an accessible Copy selection control, native copy and focused platform shortcuts that use the originating terminal's selection even after exit or disconnection. Preserve Ctrl+C interruption without selection, paste framing, duplicate-event prevention and session replacement checks.

When browser clipboard writes are unavailable or rejected, attempt supported fallbacks and offer the captured text in a normal selectable field. Report success only after a successful copy, retain the user's selection and keep asynchronous results attached to their originating tab. Do not disrupt input or focus in another tab. Custom Skills now use the shared agent-tab lifecycle, so test that surface explicitly as well as ordinary Agent tabs.

Reconcile tests with current main f880b776 and its browser-fixture and rendered-output fixes. The old candidate's tests/support/web_app.js and test-file restructuring are not authoritative; retain only changes needed for this behavior. Run focused browser checks with actual Chromium and report any skips as skips. Verify selection gestures, copy after exit, denied clipboard access, tab switching, keyboard focus, interruption, exactly-once paste and retained rendering against the final candidate using current Skill verification.

This is a recovery Round following the Skills review on 10 September 2026. Start from current main in a new managed Round worktree. Preserve Round 1, its plans, logs, branches, commits and uncommitted files; inspect and selectively reuse useful work instead of replaying the whole old attempt. skill.name: Plan
skill.prompt:
## Plan

Produce a complete, concise implementation plan for the current Goal Round. Inspect the repository and applicable context, resolve assumptions, consider alternatives and critique your proposed solution before finalizing it. Choose the planning method appropriate to the work. For a scoped finding recovery Round, focus the plan on the requested correction against the retained candidate. Do not change repository files. Return an actionable plan with stable checklist IDs and meaningful verification.

## Intent and architecture

Applicability: Apply when a Goal changes Refine product behavior, architecture, shared capabilities, durable state, workflow, or a surface contract.

Use the Goal and the relevant files under docs/intent/ as the durable product context. Preserve the Model, Application, Infrastructure, and Surfaces boundaries; shared capability ownership; thin and semantically consistent surfaces; local inspectable state; and recoverable Git and process behavior. Update only the affected docs/intent pages when the change alters documented product intent or an architectural contract. Do not require unrelated documentation, cleanup, or broader work.

For this project on the current Default node, /home/buddy/projects/refine-next is the target development checkout and /home/buddy/projects/refine is the serving Refine installation. Use the invocation's pinned workspace (the managed Goal Round worktree when supplied) for code changes and verification, and read the relevant intent from that candidate. Verify paths from the current invocation and runtime before operating on another node. Source promotion and restarting the serving installation are separate operator actions; an ordinary implementation or Quality run should not deploy its candidate or restart the daemon that is supervising it.

## Cohesive code files

Applicability: Apply whenever an agent adds or changes code files in any language.

Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.
